title: Dwelling at the Root of a Tree
html:
• Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.183 Numbered Discourses 5.183
  • 19. Araññavagga 19. Wilderness Dwellers

Rukkhamūlikasutta Dwelling at the Root of a Tree

“Pañcime, bhikkhave, rukkhamūlikā. “Mendicants, there are these five who dwell at the root of a tree. Katame pañca? What five? Mandattā momūhattā rukkhamūliko hoti …pe… idamatthitaṁyeva nissāya rukkhamūliko hoti. One may dwell at the root of a tree because of stupidity … corrupt wishes … madness … because it is praised by the Buddhas … or for the sake of having few wishes … Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca rukkhamūlikā”ti. These are the five who dwell at the root of a tree.”

Tatiyaṁ.
